Sarika and Lalremsiami, two young women who are roommates and close friends since first year, came in together today. Last month each came alone, each describing the other as the problem: one "always nagging," one "always disappearing."
Today they were calmer. I asked them to describe a recent bad evening step by step. Halfway through, Lalremsiami stopped and said, "When you keep asking what's wrong, I hide in my headphones. And then you ask more."
Sarika said, "And when you hide, I panic and ask more." They both laughed, a bit embarrassed.
I drew a circle on the whiteboard and wrote their two sentences on it. I asked them to bring the drawing back next week with one idea for breaking it.

Sunday

Sarika and I had the best talk we've had in months. Not a fight. A talk.

It happened on the college steps after the play. We were both tired and in a good mood, and she said, "Can I say something without us fighting?"

She said: "When you go quiet, I get scared, so I push." I said: "And when you push, I panic, so I go quieter." We both laughed, because it was so obvious once it was out loud. Like a see-saw.

Then she said something I've been thinking about all evening: "Maybe it's not you or me. It's the see-saw."

So we gave it a name. When it starts, either of us can just say "see-saw," and we stop and check.

I feel lighter tonight than in weeks.

Asif
